name: SQLite
model: Tables of rows queried with SQL, the whole database in one ordinary file; flexible column typing unless tables are declared STRICT
engine_note: A library linked into your process; each table and index is a B-tree in one file; rollback journal by default, write-ahead log (WAL) mode optional
consistency: Multi-row transactions. Serializable, because only one writer at a time holds the database lock (in WAL mode readers see a snapshot while one writer works). Default synchronous=FULL syncs to disk on commit. No built-in replication.
scaling: One file on one machine; scales up only. Many readers, one writer at a time. Replication needs add-ons (Litestream, LiteFS, rqlite) or a hosted service (Turso, Cloudflare D1).
reach: Reach for it for a local app, a CLI tool, tests, an edge device, or a single-server site where one process owns the data.
avoid: Avoid when many servers must write the same data over a network, or when writes are heavily concurrent.
escape: You leave the Postgres default for this because you want no server at all: the database is a file inside your process.
chat: A desktop or on-device copy of a user's chat history; or test fixtures. Not the shared production store.
notes: deploy is embedded only; Turso and Cloudflare D1 are services built on SQLite (Turso on its libSQL fork), not SQLite itself. Public domain dedication, so licence_class set to permissive.
